blogs.title: The Ternary Revolution: How BitNet b1.58 Packs Large Language Models into 1.58 Bits
blogs.description: An introductory deep‑dive that explains what a "1‑bit" LLM really is, why the authors added a zero value to create ternary weights, and how this modest change (‑1, 0, +1) leads to the surprising claim that every parameter can be stored in just 1.58 bits while retaining full expressive power.

blogs.title: Same Accuracy, Half the Bits – Inside the Training Tricks That Let b1.58 Match FP16
blogs.description: A technical walk‑through of the quantization pipeline used in BitNet b1.58—abs‑mean scaling, RoundClip rounding, and the switch to 8‑bit activations—showing how these tricks enable training from scratch and still achieve parity with FP16 LLaMA baselines on perplexity and zero‑shot benchmarks.

blogs.title: Scaling Law Redefined: Why a 13B BitNet Beats a 3B FP16 Model in Speed and Memory
blogs.description: Explains the new scaling law introduced by the authors, illustrating with concrete numbers how a 13 B parameter BitNet b1.58 is faster, uses less GPU memory, and consumes far less energy than a traditional 3 B FP16 model—and how this trend only grows stronger at larger scales.

blogs.title: Energy‑Smart AI: From Matrix Multiplications to Integer Additions
blogs.description: Breaks down the energy model behind 1‑bit LLMs, comparing integer additions versus floating‑point multiplications, and quantifies the reported 71× reduction in arithmetic‑operation energy on modern silicon (7 nm). The post highlights why power is now the bottleneck for AI chips.

blogs.title: Edge‑Ready Language Models: Deploying 1‑Bit LLMs on Mobile and Embedded Devices
blogs.description: Translates the paper's findings into practical implications for smartphones, IoT gadgets, and low‑power CPUs—showcasing how trimming weights to ternary values trims RAM footprints and enables real‑time inference that was previously only possible on data‑center GPUs.

blogs.title: Future Chipsets for Ternary AI: Designing Hardware Optimized for BitNet‑Style Models
blogs.description: Looks ahead at hardware opportunities opened by eliminating multiplications—discusses concepts like LPUs from Groq, proposes specialized SRAM/DRAM hierarchies for ternary weights, and outlines what an ideal "1‑bit" accelerator could look like for both inference and training.
